'''Thomas William Edmondson''' (June 26, 1869 – November 5, 1938) was an American [[mathematician]]. He was a physics and mathematics professor at [[New York University]] from 1896 to his retirement in 1934.

==Early life==
Thomas William Edmondson was born on June 26, 1869, in [[Skipton|Skipton-in-Craven]], [[Yorkshire]], [[England]], to Sarah (née Dodgson) and Thomas Edmondson Sr.<ref name="guide">{{cite web |url=http://dlib.nyu.edu/findingaids/html/archives/edmondson/bioghist.html|title=Biography|work=Guide to the Thomas William Edmondson Papers MC 17|publisher=New York University Library Archives|first=Barbara J.|last=Balliet|date=January 1978|accessdate=2026-03-16}}</ref><ref name="obit2">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-ottawa-citizen-dr-thomas-edmondson/193537391/ |title=Dr. Thomas Edmondson Dies at Mount Vernon |date=1938-11-07 |newspaper=The Evening Citizen |page=14 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2026-03-16}}{{Open access}}</ref> His father was a printer and publisher.<ref name="obit3">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/craven-herald-and-pioneer-distinguished/193538326/ |title=Distinguished Skiptonian |date=1938-11-18 |newspaper=Craven Herald and Pioneer |page=11 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2026-03-16}}{{Open access}}</ref>

Edmondson attended elementary school in Skipton. He attended [[Skipton Grammar School]] and was a head boy.<ref name="guide"/><ref name="obit3"/> He graduated from the [[University of London]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in 1888. He received the Ackroyd Scholarship and attended the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="guide"/><ref name="obit3"/><ref name="obit2"/> In 1891, he graduated from Cambridge with a Bachelor of Arts and received the 18th wrangler mark in the [[Mathematical Tripos]].<ref name="guide"/><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-guardian-prof-t-w-edmondson-18-n/193537908/ |title=Prof. T. W. Edmondson |date=1938-11-18 |newspaper=The Manchester Guardian |page=6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2026-03-16}}{{Open access}}</ref> He then worked as an assistant tutor in mathematics and physics at Cambridge's University Correspondence College.<ref name="guide"/> In 1893, he left England for America. He graduated from [[Clark University]] with a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in 1896.<ref name="guide"/><ref name="obit3"/><ref name="obit">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/mount-vernon-argus-professor-dies-at-69/193535776/ |title=Professor Dies at 69 |date=1938-11-05 |newspaper=Mount Vernon Argus |page=2 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2026-03-16}}{{Open access}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1896, Edmondson joined [[New York University]] as an assistant professor of physics. He worked alongside Daniel W. Hering. He also assisted Pomeroy Ladue in the mathematics department. In 1903, he became an assistant professor of mathematics.<ref name="guide"/><ref name="obit3"/><ref name="obit"/> He took over as head of the mathematics department following Ladue's retirement in 1906. He remained as department head until his retirement on August 31, 1934.<ref name="guide"/><ref name="obit3"/><ref name="obit"/> He was acting dean of the New York University graduate school from 1916 to 1921.<ref name="obit2"/><ref name="obit3"/> He was secretary of the faculty committee of the university council from 1903 to 1933.<ref name="guide"/>  He was chairman of the Washington Square Collegiate Division in 1913.<ref name="guide"/> He also served as college bursar, treasurer of the athletic association, and was a member of the Beta chapter of [[Phi Beta Kappa]].<ref name="obit3"/>

Edmondson was a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]], the American Mathematical Association, the [[American Association of University Professors]], and the [[English Place-Name Society]].<ref name="obit3"/><ref name="obit"/> He was a member of the Craven Naturalists and Scientific Association.<ref name="obit3"/>

==Personal life==
Edmondson married Minnie Ramsden of [[Perth, Ontario]], in 1896. They had no children.<ref name="guide"/><ref name="obit3"/><ref name="obit2"/> He lived on Franklin Avenue in [[Mount Vernon, New York]].<ref name="obit"/> He attended the First Baptist Church in Mount Vernon.<ref name="obit"/> His hobbies included [[botany]] and archaeological research.<ref name="obit3"/>

Edmondson died on November 4, 1938, at Mount Vernon Hospital.<ref name="obit"/>

==Works==
Edmondson wrote books on topics, including spark discharge in dielectrics; potential, spherical harmonic analysis; and on curves and elliptic functions.<ref name="obit2"/>

His publications included:{{citation needed |date=March 2026}}  
* ''Worked Examples in Coördinate Geometry'' (1891)  
* ''Mensuration and Spherical Geometry'' (1893), with W. Briggs  
* ''Deductions in Euclid'' (1901)
